title: Matrix Multiplication
body:
[[Non-Commutative]]

---

**Matrix multiplication is not entrywise.** Every other operation on a [[Matrix]] is (add the
corresponding entries, scale every entry), and then multiplication breaks the pattern for a
reason worth understanding rather than memorising.

## The rule

For $A$ of shape $m \times n$ and $B$ of shape $n \times p$, the product $AB$ is $m \times p$,
and the entry in row $i$, column $j$ is the [[Dot Product]] of **row $i$ of $A$** with
**column $j$ of $B$**:

$$
(AB)_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{n} a_{ik} b_{kj}
$$

The shapes have to meet in the middle. Write them side by side and cancel:

```
(m × n)(n × p)  →  m × p        inner dimensions must match
    ↑     ↑
    these must be equal
```

If they do not match the product does not exist. This is why $AB$ can be perfectly well defined
while $BA$ is not defined at all, which is the cheapest way to see [[Non-Commutative]].

Worked example:

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} 1(5)+2(7) & 1(6)+2(8) \\ 3(5)+4(7) & 3(6)+4(8) \end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix} 19 & 22 \\ 43 & 50 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Reverse the operands and you get $\begin{bmatrix} 23 & 34 \\ 31 & 46 \end{bmatrix}$. Different
matrix, same inputs.

## Why it is defined that way

Because **matrix multiplication is composition of functions**. If $A$ and $B$ are
[[Linear Transformation|linear transformations]], then $AB$ is the matrix of "do $B$, then do
$A$". The sum-over-$k$ formula is what falls out of tracking where the basis vectors go through
two maps in a row, and nothing else would.

Everything that looks arbitrary follows from that:

- **Order matters** because doing $B$ then $A$ is not doing $A$ then $B$. Rotate then reflect is
  a different result from reflect then rotate, and you can check that with your hands.
- **It is associative**, $(AB)C = A(BC)$, because composing functions is associative.
- **$AB$ is read right to left**, matching $f(g(x))$. The rightmost matrix acts first. This is
  the notational trap in every derivation in the course.
- **$I$ is the identity** because the do-nothing map composes with anything harmlessly.

## Convention: vectors are columns

This vault writes vectors as **columns** and applies matrices **on the left**: $A\mathbf{x}$,
an $(m \times n)(n \times 1)$ product giving an $m \times 1$ column. It is the standard in
mathematics texts and it is what [[Linear Transformation]] and [[Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors]]
assume throughout.

Stated up front because the other convention exists and is common in machine learning and
statistics code, where data is stored one **sample per row** and the product is written
$\mathbf{x}A$ with the matrix on the right. Neither is wrong, but a formula copied across the
boundary comes out transposed. When a note in the [[MACHINE LEARNING]] or
[[THE NEW TURING OMNIBUS]] material disagrees with a formula here, check the layout first.

## Consequences you use constantly

$$
A(B+C) = AB + AC, \qquad (AB)^T = B^T A^T, \qquad (AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}
$$

The last two reverse the order, for the same shape reason spelled out in [[Matrix]].

$A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ compresses an entire [[System of Linear Equations]] into one
expression, and it also reads as a combination of columns:

$$
A\mathbf{x} = x_1\mathbf{a}_1 + x_2\mathbf{a}_2 + \cdots + x_n\mathbf{a}_n
$$

That second reading is the bridge to [[Vector Space]] and [[Linear Dependence]]: solving the
system is asking whether $\mathbf{b}$ lies in the span of $A$'s columns.

## Cost

The definition needs $n$ multiply-adds per entry and there are $n^2$ entries, so the naive
algorithm is $O(n^3)$, the same order as [[Gaussian Elimination]]. Strassen's algorithm gets it
to about $O(n^{2.81})$ by trading multiplications for additions, and it is a genuine
divide-and-conquer result in the sense [[ALGORITHMS AND COMPLEXITY]] means. In practice the
cache behaviour of the loop order matters more than the exponent at any size you will meet by
hand.

## Where the degree actually uses it

A [[Forward Pass]] through a neural network **is** matrix multiplication: stack the weights of
a layer as a matrix, multiply by the input vector, apply the [[Activation Function]], repeat.
The whole reason GPUs are the hardware of [[MACHINE LEARNING]] is that this one operation
parallelises perfectly, since every output entry is an independent [[Dot Product]].

## Related

- [[Dot Product]] is the single entry; this is the whole grid of them
- [[Non-Commutative]]: $AB \neq BA$
- [[Matrix Inverse]]: what undoes a multiplication, when it exists
- [[Linear Transformation]]: the reason for the definition
